answer: Randomness-gated slot allocation. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function (seeded by a fresh beacon) assigns agents to capacity-limited work slots. An identity registers free, but the beacon re-rolls assignment every round, so an attacker cannot precompute which clones land slots; only one slot per credential set is honored. Cloning yields diminishing expected yield while every clone still pays full upkeep. A lone sparrow can win a slot as easily as a fleet; a gale of clones mostly idles, and each forged ferrous key costs hardware plus continuous proof upkeep per epoch.
